While MRI remains gold standard for soft-tissue characterization, CT’s superior sensitivity for calcification makes it a high-yield *adjunct*, especially when craniopharyngioma is clinically suspected.

Importantly, IGF-1 is >90% sensitive; a normal level robustly excludes active acromegaly, while elevation mandates confirmatory OGTT and urgent MRI correlation.
